title: Ink DOM-level ScrollBox substrate
objective: Introduce a Swarm-owned DOM-level scroll/render substrate modeled on cc's ScrollBox so long-session scrolling can bypass React state churn and support sticky scroll, pending delta, clamp bounds, and viewport culling.
actions: Create a Swarm TUI scroll primitive with imperative `scrollTo`, `scrollBy`, `scrollToBottom`, `isSticky`, `subscribe`, and clamp-bound APIs.
Keep scroll position and pending wheel/page deltas in the rendered node or a stable external store rather than React state.
Support sticky-scroll behavior for streaming output while allowing manual scroll to break stickiness.
Expose fresh viewport and content-height reads for later virtual-list and search behavior.
Integrate the primitive behind `ConversationFullscreenLayout` without changing the default conversation presentation yet.

criteria: Scroll mutations no longer require updating React state per scroll event.
Sticky bottom behavior remains correct while assistant output streams.
Manual scroll breaks stickiness and preserves the user's viewport.
Tests cover scrollTo, scrollBy, sticky bottom, pending delta, and clamp-bound behavior.
Existing TUI tests still pass with the new primitive present but minimally integrated.

non_goals: Do not rewrite the entire Ink renderer in one task.
Do not migrate message virtualization before the ScrollBox API is covered by tests.
Do not change Gateway, Symphony, LSP, or cache behavior in this task.
findings: Added Swarm-owned ScrollBox substrate with external mutable scroll controller, sticky bottom, pending delta, clamp bounds, window reads, and minimal ConversationFullscreenLayout integration without changing default transcript presentation.
